# Manor: room-by-room emotional progression (Track M, v1.1)

**Aim:** a royal candlelit home that is crafted, playful and tactile, and shares only three things with the Front Door: one accent, one typeface, one spring table.

## The curve
Welcome, anticipation, reverence, curiosity, intimacy, wonder, play. Each step changes scale, temperature and tempo so no two rooms feel alike. Workshop is cut (not in the north star; models move to the Hall).

## Rooms (mood = ZoneMood.Make skyTop, horizon, sun, shade, sunIntensity, fogDensity/start; fill is assigned after Make)
1. **Foyer, "Threshold" (beat 1).** Warm, open, brightest room. Ivory plaster, limestone tile, red carpet, brass. `#1B2140 #3B2622 #FFB46A #33284A 0.72 0.020/12`. Moment: candles light in a wave along the carpet as you walk, flames popping on the settle spring; the name sits on a brass-bracket plaque. Touch: the two low pedestals.
2. **Grand Gallery, "The Long Look" (beats 2, 3).** Three bays split by arches; the two best works large on a focal wall. Prussian walls (Cyanotype, no lattice), oak herringbone, walnut. `#141A33 #2A1C20 #FFAE5E #2B2646 0.60 0.018/14`. Moment: stand on a brass floor marker and the project "develops" from blue to colour with a small FOV kick (the game's own develop and kick). Surprise: frames without content show a Frost "coming soon" slide, never pink fog.
3. **Hall of Honours, "Reverence" (beat 3).** About 9 m tall, apse, walnut sides dim, limestone backdrop bright, terrazzo floor with brass dividers. `#171A2E #2C2230 #FFE3B8 #2A2540 0.95 0.016/16`, sun near vertical. Moment: statues emerge from fog on the centre line and are top-lit; E at a plate turns a statue a quarter turn on the weight spring. [PLACEHOLDER: awards and medals].
4. **Camera Room (beat 4).** Graphite walls, oak boards, one Frost light table as the only cool light. `#10121F #3A1E14 #DCEBFF #241E36 0.35 0.030/8`. Moment: lift the camera, turn the lens ring, a film look blends in and a print ejects with a pop. Needs a per-mood grade seam.
5. **Study, "Hearth" (beat 3).** Small, low, all walnut, terracotta hearth. `#1A1420 #34201A #FF9C4A #30203A 0.50 0.034/7`. Moment: light the candle on the desk (E); the room blends up over 2 s and the contact letter appears. [PLACEHOLDER: contact and about].
6. **Painting Wing, "Moonlit" (beat 4).** The only cool room: pale plaster, limestone, Starry Night blues. `#25376A #3E5C8D #C4CB8E #1B2447 0.55 0.012/18`. Moment: walk into the frame; brushwork swirls as you approach, a Frost flash (0.30) covers the cut, Track G takes over.
7. **Arcade Parlour (beats 3, 4).** Red salon, teal and mustard seating, cabinets in a horseshoe, their screens the main light. `#1E1020 #3A1626 #FFC27A #3A1F40 0.55 0.022/10`. Moment: drop a brass coin (E at the slot, pop spring), then the existing arcade overlay opens.

## Styles and Mats
All from existing Mats (ManorLook.cs:39-52): Brass is already within 1.08:1 of the ref gilt. Optional up/palette requests, ranked: crimson Silk, Glass (statue cases), Marble. None block Wave 1b.

## Identity bridge
- **Accent:** Brass #C59A45. 7.35:1 on #140E10, 4.20:1 on Graphite, 2.19:1 on paper (measured), so on a light Front Door use it as a fill or a point, not text.
- **Type:** Nunito ExtraBold and SemiBold (shipped, OFL) plus the [ ] bracket motif.
- **Springs:** settle 2.6 Hz/0.82, lag 1.8/0.75, weight 1.2/0.90 (proposed). For JS, mass 1: k 266.9, c 26.79; k 127.9, c 16.96; k 56.8, c 13.57.

## Fix today, ranked
1. Upstream pale boot card sits between landing and Manor (third identity).
2. Gallery is one tube of eight identical frames.
3. Placeholder paintings look like unfinished fog.
4. Wallpaper lattice and one-note Candlelight mood; fill is grey, so ceiling, wainscot and carpet merge.
5. Candles repeat every 8 m; far doors vanish in fog.
6. Arcade cabinet is flat on the wall with no spill light.

## Cuts and risks
Cut Workshop, lattice, repeated sconces, the gallery alcove. Risk: seven Manor zones plus painting worlds all build at boot (unmeasured). Flag: confirm the accent and the [ ] monogram with the owner.

# Manor floor plan and curation (m02-architect, north star v1.1)

## Shape: an enfilade spine
Foyer -> Grand Gallery -> {Hall of Honours, Camera Room -> Painting Wing -> Worlds}. The Gallery is the only hub. Maximum depth from the Gallery is 3 doors. Every room has a [ GRAND GALLERY ] door within 3 m of arrival (GoToZone lets a door place you at a chosen spot, GameBootstrap.cs:330-336), plus a hotkey from anywhere, plus a return path out of the game (missing seam, fork-map section 9).

## Zones (X line, index*50)
| key | order/idx/x | footprint (x by z, height) | job |
|---|---|---|---|
| pf.foyer | 1000/6/300 | 18 x 24, 6 m | identity, contact bureau, doors |
| pf.gallery | 1010/7/350 | 15 x 48, 8 m | 8 frames, Tribune statue, arcade |
| pf.honours | 1020/8/400 | 16 x 44, 12 m | hero statue, 6 awards, 6 medal vitrines |
| pf.lens | 1030/9/450 | 16 x 32, 9 m | X-T5 monument, 5 lenses, 4 film looks |
| pf.wing | 1040/10/500 | 12 x 34, 7 m | framed portals |
| pf.world.starry | 1100/11/550 | 40 x 120, open | the pilot world |
| pf.world.bedroom | 1101/12/600 | 10 x 12 | coda, skewed room |

All closed rooms stay within +-9 m of their root, well inside the +-25 m limit. Worlds sit last so only the closed Wing draws as a silhouette; a ridge on the world's west edge hides it. Key pf.lens avoids a clash with the core 'camera' zone in debug lookups.

## Routes (4.5 m/s, no sprint, FirstPersonController.cs:78; model in the evidence folder)
- **Fast, 39 s:** Foyer straight to the Gallery door (7 s), nave to z=26 with three stops on the best frames (20 s), Tribune (6 s).
- **Everything, 134 s:** Foyer contact 13 s, 8 frames 48 s, Tribune and door 10 s, Hall (hero, 6 awards, 6 medals) 63 s. 46 s of slack to the 180 s gate.
- **Explorer:** arcade (E), Hall, Camera Room (take a lens, print a photo), Wing, Starry Night, Café Terrace, Bedroom, back through a gilt frame. Rewards: snuffable candelabras (typed idea), a framed plan of the house that opens the overlay map.

## Curation
Wall frame = projects. Marble plinth = statues and awards. Podium/turntable = Blender models and lenses. Vitrine = medals. Niche = hero backdrop, film looks. Stele = monogram, roll of honour. Easel = prints. Cabinet = playable demos. Glass and gilt Mats need the up/palette seam.

## Hall of Honours numbers
Hero 4.8 m on a 1.5 m plinth (6.3 m), ceiling 12 m (1.9x), first-view inlay at 14 m, plaque at 4 m. Awards 2.2 m on 0.9 m plinths, 6 m from the carpet. Pedestal ratio and 12-16 m distance are estimates, not documented.

## Painting Wing
Frames on a 4.3 m bay grid, every other bay, staggered so none face each other. Canvas 3.2 x 2.56 m (Starry Night aspect 1.25). Cross the brass inlay: FOV punch, 2 s mood blend, zone swap. Return frame in each world lands you in front of the same painting. Image = diorama photo of the world itself (the allowed texture).

## Budgets (estimates unless marked; caps keep >= 17% headroom)
Measured: foyer 73 batches / 18,664 tris, gallery 63 / 40,292. Caps: foyer 85/24k, gallery 80/47k, hall 95/50k, lens 85/40k, wing 75/35k, starry 100/50k, bedroom 50/15k. Gallery pays for the Tribune by dropping chandeliers to 8 candles.

## Walk spots (local, y=0, on carpet, off plinths)
Foyer (0,10),(0,16.5); Gallery (0,16),(0,34); Hall (0,10),(0,20),(0,30); Lens (0,10),(0,20); Wing (0,6),(0,16),(0,24); Starry (0,10),(0,40),(0,80). Teleport steps via Destination, as ManorRooms.cs:132.

## Delete first under pressure
Bedroom zone, then fold Camera Room into the Wing, then worlds beyond Starry, then halve the Hall plinths.

## Uncertain
New-room budgets are estimates. Cross-zone preview access is unverified. Hall and Gallery shell height changes touch the shared ManorHall helper.

# Hall of Honours heroes (m05-statues, north star v1.1)

**Decision:** four code-built monuments, built in this order: DECA glass award, medal gantry, camera monument, robot/CAD statue. Blender is deferred; no authored mesh is needed to hit the look or the budget.

## The four

| # | Object | Height | Reads at 12 m | 3 m | 1 m |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **DECA glass award** | 4.25 m (plinth 1.25, glass 2.7 x 1.1 x 0.16) | a cold-white blade with clipped top corners, glowing in a warm room | amber bevels and brass rails | bracket clips, diamond emblem, plaque |
| 2 | **Medal gantry** (3 shown, up to 5) | 3.4 m, discs 1.0 m | a row of discs at staggered heights, V-ribbons rising to a crossbar, open gap beneath | rim beads (Ultra), star emblem | ribbon fold, eyelet |
| 3 | **Camera monument** (X-T5-style, 16x) | 2.7 m, 2.08 m wide | stepped top-plate skyline: EVF hump plus dials, round lens, grip bulge | lens rings, dials | plinth print: a photo of this hall |
| 4 | **Robot/CAD statue** (exploded assembly) | 3.5 m | five floating plates, four chunky wheels, one diagonal arm | brass leader rods and arrows | standoffs, chips, plaque |

Meaning: 1 and 2 are beat 3 (every award and medal). 3 is beat 4 (the owner builds cameras and worlds) and matches the owner's "fujifilm x5 style" camera; 4 is beat 3 and 4 (robot and CAD exhibits). No logos or brand text on the camera.

## Method
Everything uses `PropBuild` primitives (`Box`, `Chamfer`, `Prism`, `Wedge`, `Beam`) plus two fork-side convex helpers, `Frustum(sides, topRatio)` and `ClippedHull(size, planes)`, which copy the `ArchMeshes.Chamfered` pattern and go through `Arch.Piece`. Every piece is closed and convex, so it bakes, batches, is photographed, cut and pasted like the rest of the world. Bodies are Soft; only plinths are Solid (one Mat).

**Deferred authored path:** a `HeroMeshBaker` would take FBX/GLB children named `Mat__Pat__part` (each a closed convex solid), split normals, white vertex colour, `Geo.SetNoPattern`, `Arch.Piece`, then the zone bake writes UV0. Non-convex parts go under an `Interactable` (Device, never cut). No `.blend`, no LFS; any third-party base is CC0/CC-BY, credited in CREDITS.md. Needed only for the owner's real robot CAD later.

## Cheap glass, no local lights
Glass is `Mat.Frost` (self-lit 0.82, never blooms): a glowing pane, not transparency. The shader has no specular, so brightness comes from bevels: with the Candlelight sun at (0.22, 0.92, -0.30), a 45 degree top bevel gets N.L about 0.85 against about 0.30 on the doorway-facing front, so bevels read amber against cool faces on Low, Med and High. Rules: bevels at least 0.08 m, brass rails against Frost/Graphite, 4 to 5 distinct values per object, 12 to 24 sided rounds. Ultra only adds twin detail (dentils, knurls, etch lines) plus the 8 nearest existing lights; heroes carry no `LocalLights`.

## Materials
Frost (glass), Brass (gilt), Limestone + Terrazzo/Ashlar (plinth), Graphite, Concrete (silver stand-in), Terracotta, TextileRed, Cyanotype. Optional `up/palette` request: append **Silver** and **Crystal**. Not required.

## Cost (derived from source; no Unity run)
| Object | Tris | Ultra extra | Audited batches |
|---|---|---|---|
| DECA | 604 | 240 | 4 |
| Medals (5) | 1,848 | 576 | 4 |
| Robot | 1,096 | 192 | 2 |
| Camera | 1,286 | 720 | 2 |
| **Heroes** | **4,834** | **+1,728 = 6,562** | **12** |

Hall shell estimate 13,400 tris, 55 to 84 batches (estimate). Total about 20k tris at 1x, about 40k even at 2.5x shell error (cap 60k; 20% headroom line 48k). **Batches are the binding limit:** 84 + 12 = 96 = exactly 80% of 120, so the Hall shell must measure at most 84. Labels (uGUI) are real draws not counted by `Arch.Audit`; one plaque per hero.

## Placeholders
Brass plaque `[ PLACEHOLDER: event, placement, year ]` in the same bracket idiom as `[ GRAND GALLERY ]`. The glass shows a geometric diamond, never text. Medals read `[ PLACEHOLDER: medal name ]`; metals are slot-based, not rank claims.

## Hand-off (M-C1, `Assets/Portfolio/Runtime/Exhibits/**`)
`HeroKit.GlassAward / MedalGantry / RobotStatue / CameraMonument / Plinth` with `(Transform p, Vector3 basePos, Dir facing, HeroSpec spec)`; `HeroKit.Audit(go)` returns an `Arch.ArtAudit`. PlayMode `HeroKitTests`: builds with `ctx.Game == null`; `Arch.Validate` passes; per-hero batch and tri caps; zero `Light` components; heights within 5%; placeholder text starts with `[PLACEHOLDER`.

## Cut / uncertain
Cut: Blender in Wave 1, real transparency, animation, robot first if over budget. Uncertain: Hall shell cost (estimate), Hall height 6 vs 8 m, DECA real shape, and Blender not connected this session.

# Look Dev: materials and candlelight (m06-lookdev)

North star v1.1. Recon only; every number marked estimate has not been run in Unity.

## The problem (measured from Build/shots/gallery-spawn.png)
Flames are flat yellow prisms (ManorKit.cs:25). Brass and candelabras read as flat amber (FlatToon has no specular and forces one tone per face, FlatToon.shader:10-11, Palette.cs:261-265). The floor is the coolest, flattest surface in a warm room. Below Ultra, nothing lights anything: the only light is a 0.56 "sun" and dim ambient (ManorLook.cs:23-28).

## Decisions
1. **Light pools in the shader, every tier.** Eight pools (`_IonPoolPos/_IonPoolCol[8]`) added to FlatToon ForwardLit before fog (after FlatToon.shader:368). Toon-banded, half-lambert wrapped, no geometry, no batch, no light. A fork-only feeder (`Assets/Portfolio/Runtime/ManorGlow.cs`) picks the nearest N per frame (Low 4, Med/High 8) with smoothed fades. Flicker +/-8%, 0 under reduced motion. Decals and vertex-colour pools are cut (z-fight, saturated vertex colour at FlatToon.shader:298).
2. **Gilt is a finish, not a hex.** Brass and the reference gilt are the same colour. `_Finish` mode 1 gives a 3-step reflection ramp with a hard horizon line; on Med+ a sparkle toward the nearest pool. Brass stays for markers.
3. **Glass is opaque.** Mat.Glass (dark #2E3F47) plus Pat.Glint (two diagonal bands), on an unglazed Gilt frame. No blended pane: PhotoDisplay is a UGUI shader (PhotoDisplay.shader:28-50), blended panes add sorting and overdraw, and the slicer cuts opaque pieces. Cost: +1 batch, 0 overdraw.
4. **Marble and velvet.** Pat.Marble (domain-warped veins as a luma multiplier, world-anchored, fades with the existing 25-45 m pattern fade). Velvet is a fresnel sheen with its own colour, because the stock rim uses the near-black sky ambient (FlatToon.shader:329-340).
5. **Flame** = Mat.Flame (#FF9A3C) outer cone around the Warm core. No billboards.
6. **Ultra's 8 lights** go to chandeliers, candelabras and teleporters only. Sconces lose their real light (ManorKit.cs:91). Foyer: 2 chandeliers + 4 candelabras + 2 teleporters = 8. Gallery: 13 candidates, nearest 8. Real intensity halves, since pools already carry the diffuse look.
7. **Anti-mud rule.** Cool plum-blue fog (#1C1A2E), key yellow-white at the flame, orange only in falloff, warm pools about 35% of frame.

## Palette seam (up/palette; Lead A)
New Mats, append-only: Gilt 24 #CFA24A, Marble 25 #E6E1D8, Velvet 26 #8B1A2B, Glass 27 #2E3F47, Flame 28 #FF9A3C (emission 0.9, self-lit 1), Silver 29 #C4CAD3 (deferred). New Pats: Marble 18, Glint 19.
Files: Surface.cs:15,27,61; Palette.cs:177,201-225,252-265; FlatToon.shader (properties 29-49, CBUFFER 67-89, pool and finish blocks near 346-370); IonPattern.hlsl:36,322-326,345-356; IonAudio.Footsteps.cs:33-87.
Tests that must stay green: ArchKitTests.cs:68-91 (every Mat round trip), PatternUVTests.cs:93-101, AudioTests.cs:97, ArtPlayTests.cs:20-56, UltraPlayTests.cs:51, ZoneCatalogTests.cs:52. Add: finish-property test, Pat decode to Glint, pool-count test.

## Costs (estimates)
Batches: about +3 net (Marble, Glass, Flame; Gilt and Velvet replace Brass, Mustard, TextileRed). Triangles: negligible. GPU: pool loop about 8 x 20 ALU on all FlatToon pixels, 4 on Low; profile before shipping. Low: pools + ramp only. Med+: sparkle. Ultra: real lights + bloom.

## Moods (fork-only, ManorLook.cs)
See roleOutput.moods. Assumed rooms, since no Creative Director list existed.

## Uncertainty and cuts
Radii, flicker and coverage are unmeasured. Floor style conflict between screenshot (Checker) and ManorLook.cs:41 (Oak). Cut: translucent shells, billboard flames, decals, Silver first pass, picture-light cones.

decisions.choice: Five primes by 35mm diagonal-equivalent: 16 mm (FovY 78.1), 28 mm (50, default, exactly 27.84 mm-eq), 50 mm (29.1), 85 mm (17.4), 135 mm (11.0). One pure function ViewFovFor(fovY) = clamp(2*atan(tan(fovY/2)*tan35/tan25), 20, 88) drives the view while the viewfinder is raised AND while a photo is raised. It returns exactly 70 for 50, so default behaviour is unchanged. The viewfinder and PhotoOverlayUI read a new FirstPersonController.ViewFov instead of BaseFieldOfView, and mouse look scales by tan(ViewFov/2)/tan(Base/2).
decisions.why: Today the frame fraction is tan(fov/2) over tan(70/2) (ViewfinderFrame.cs:236, PhotoOverlayUI.cs:347). A 78 degree photo in a 70 degree view overflows the screen, and a 11 degree lens at 70 degrees is a postage stamp. Placement uses only camera pose (ProjectionSystem.cs:358), so zooming the view never changes what is cut. decisions.choice: Live in IonGrade (IonAtmosphere.hlsl:110-129) behind a uniform branch, via 3 float4 globals (_IonFilmR/G/B = row coefficients, w = offset) and _IonFilmP (x contrast, y grain, z reserved, w mix 0..1). The preview camera renders through the same shaders (GradientSky.shader:109, FlatToon.shader:371, Backdrop.shader:133), so the look is baked into the print with no change to ProjectionSystem. decisions.why: One source of truth, zero extra passes and zero textures, the same pattern as the rewind look (IonAtmosphere.hlsl:95-115, one uniform branch). Alternative considered: a PhotoDisplay-side filter. It cannot be seen live in the viewfinder, so it was rejected.

decisions.choice: Capture-time accumulation DoF: re-render the preview N times (Low 0, Med 4, High 8, Ultra 12) from jittered positions on a Vogel disk of radius r = 0.5*focalMm/fNumber/1000*Gain (Gain about 6, to tune), using an off-axis shear so the autofocus plane (centre raycast, 8 m fallback) stays fixed. Blend each sample on the GPU with 1/k alpha into one RT, ReadPixels once, one sample per frame under the 6 ms stage budget while the print develops. No depth texture needed.
decisions.why: URP depth texture is OFF (URP-Ion.asset:22, ProjectSetup.cs:192). A depth-blur needs it on the preview camera plus a pass hook, and Context7 confirmed neither RenderTextureSubElement.Depth nor WebGL2 depth sampling for this setup. Accumulation uses only RenderRequest (documented) and works on WebGL2. It costs nothing during play, and it is physically right, so it needs no art tuning of a blur kernel. Fallback is Low = no DoF (sharp print). Needs ProjectionSystem.RenderInto made internal with an optional projection matrix. Sign of the shear is settled by an EditMode test. Per-sample GPU cost is an estimate until measured.
evidence: Context7 /websites/unity3d_manual SL-CameraDepthTexture (depth texture is a global during the camera render)

# M08 Camera: validated design (north star v1.1)

## What is true today
- There is no 3D camera in hand. The viewfinder (ViewfinderFrame.cs) and the raised photo (PhotoOverlayUI.cs) are uGUI, and the view FOV is a fixed 70 (PlayerFactory.cs:55). The only 3D camera is the lectern prop at PropKit.Devices.cs:238-253.
- Both overlays size the frame as tan(fov/2) over tan(35). A wide or tele photo therefore overflows or shrinks to a stamp.
- The preview is rendered by a private RenderInto (ProjectionSystem.cs:1512): ARGB32, no MSAA, synchronous ReadPixels, and it already goes through IonGrade. The URP depth texture is off.
- The plan holds no 'Fork camera' appendix. The seam is specified from code. CameraWing.cs does not pin 50 degrees; CriticFixTests.cs:46-51 and RoomSolutionTests.cs:126 do.

## The up/lens seam
- InstantCamera.cs: keep `const CaptureFovY = 50`. Add `Lens`, `FovY`, `SetLens`, `Aperture`, `Film` and a `BeforeCapture` event. TryCapture (:171) uses `FovY`.
- ViewfinderFrame.cs: settable FovY and `ViewFov` instead of BaseFieldOfView (:224).
- FirstPersonController.cs: `ViewFov` with its own spring, applied beside the FOV kick (:441), and look scaling at :477. The existing SetFovHold belongs to the teleport swell, so it is not reused.
- PhotoOverlayUI.cs:343 reads `ViewFov`. PhotoHolder skips digit and wheel selection while in camera mode (:122-123,254).
- Feel becomes `partial` (Feel.cs:12) so lens constants join the one spring table.
- IonAtmosphere.hlsl IonGrade gains the film branch. ProjectionSystem.RenderInto becomes internal with an optional projection matrix.
- Tests: ViewFovFor(50)=70 (EditMode, new); the CriticFixTests and RoomSolutionTests pins untouched; a camera-mode wheel test.

## Lenses
28 mm is the existing shape (27.84 mm-eq). The others: 16 mm / 78.1, 50 mm / 29.1, 85 mm / 17.4, 135 mm / 11.0. ViewFovFor maps the lens to a view FOV of 88 down to 20, and returns exactly 70 for the default. It drives both camera-raise and photo-raise, so the frame always fits. Wheel = lens, Q/E = aperture, F = film look. Tele aiming needs look scaling.

## Film looks
Five 3x4 stocks live in IonGrade and spring in as the camera rises. The print bakes the look at capture, with no ProjectionSystem change. They differ in what they reveal: Mono collapses equal-luma hue pairs, Cyanotype matches the rewind look.

## Depth of field
Capture-time accumulation: 4 to 12 jittered re-renders (Low = none), off-axis shear so the focus plane stays still, GPU-blended and read back once while the print develops. No depth texture and no WebGL2 depth sampling is needed (Context7 did not confirm it). The shear sign and the cost are unmeasured.

## Viewmodel and print
- X-T5 proportions (129.5 x 91 x 63.8 mm, Fujifilm spec).
- About 1,130 body tris plus 5 lenses of about 330 each, with one lens rendered at a time: about 2.8k built and about 1.5k drawn. All estimates.
- Layer 8, so it is never captured; no shadows; hidden while raised.
- The lens swap twists off, drops and twists on over about 0.55 s on a 3.2 Hz spring. Reduced motion swaps instantly.
- The print is two quads: a Paper card in instax mini proportions and an image quad using a new `Ion/PrintDevelop` shader (develop over 2.4 s).

## Camera Room
`pf.camera` at order 1020: the camera stand plus 4 lens and 3 cartridge plinths. Each lens plinth shows a print made with that lens's FovY. Lenses are `UsableBehaviour`s, persist in PlayerPrefs, and are not rewindable.

## Cut first
The exposure triangle, continuous zoom, manual focus and a live DoF preview. Build order: seam, film looks, viewmodel, print, room, DoF.

## Open
Look names (trademarks), the X-T5 finish, whether Manor visitors may paste photos, and the F binding.

decisions.topic: Panel pointer-lock handoff, Esc and Back

# m10-interaction: Manor onboarding and DOM overlay (north star v1.1)

## What I saw (measured, live Manor, 1440x900)
The loader is the upstream polaroid on a paper grid with a 434 px, 12-row controls sheet; 8 rows are puzzle-only. Click to play locks the pointer and drops you in the candlelit foyer; the two doors sit about 14 m away with plaques unreadable at that range. No Grand Gallery skip exists before the walk. Evidence: portfolio-evidence/wave1a/m10-interaction/01..04 PNG.

## First 30 seconds
1. 0-8 s loader: polaroid develops; rows cut to walk / look / use plus 'Esc steps back out'. Two buttons: 'Enter the Manor' and 'Go straight to the Grand Gallery'.
2. 8-12 s foyer: one hint line only if the player is still for 4 s, once ever.
3. 12-30 s: carpet leads to two lit doors; exhibits answer with '[E] read'.
Always-available skip: 'M plan of the house' (Grand Gallery first), and Grand Gallery in the pause sheet. Deleted: welcome toast, blurb toasts, arcade toast, the 12-row sheet.

## Panel (placeholder content, token-driven)
Content model: slug, title, role, year, blurb, url, accent, cover, demo (all exist) plus optional links[], media[], tags[], placeholder:true (shows a visible PLACEHOLDER stamp). No invented facts.
Opens from PaintingUsable (fork-only, usable seam), range about 4.5 m. A museum wall label on the right: big exhibit number, brass rule, crop-mark corners, gilt-framed 4:3 cover, numbered links, 'Open the demo' only if a demo exists. The painting stays in view.
States: closed, opening (220 ms ease-out, 8 px rise, the game's own Feel constants), open, media-loading (accent block), placeholder, closing (160 ms). Reduced motion: opacity only.
Keys: E opens; Tab cycles inside; Esc, Back button, backdrop click, browser Back all close. Focus goes to the heading on open and back to the canvas on close.
Handoff: open releases the lock programmatically; the Back button re-locks in the same click; Esc ends at 'Click to resume' (MDN: re-lock needs a gesture).

## Map
DOM 'Plan of the house', M to open: an SVG plan with numbered hot-spots over a real ordered list of buttons (keyboard and AT path). Entries come from ZoneCatalog and PortfolioCatalog. Travel is a polled request: C# calls GoToRoom or Player.Teleport. Zero batches.

## Arcade and loader
Shared tokens (:where(:root) defaults, the site overrides): accent, display and UI fonts, ink, paper, brass, wood, scrim, focus, ease, in/out, rise, radius. Bezel: lit marquee, screen, control-deck strip. Fixes: dialog name, per-project iframe title, focus trap and inert, visible focus ring, relock on button close, postMessage Esc contract, sandbox without allow-same-origin for third-party demos.
jslib API: IonPanelOpen(json), IonPanelClose(), IonMapOpen(json), IonMapTakeRequest() -> string, IonArcadeOpen(url,title), IonArcadeClose(), IonOverlayIsOpen() -> int, IonOverlaySerial(which) -> int, IonAnnounce(text), IonPrefersReducedMotion() -> int. All wrapped in try/catch (exceptions off).

## Accessibility
Every interaction has a key path and Esc/back. First focusable: 'Read everything as a page' (Front Door). Live region mirrors the prompt and room titles. OS reduced-motion now seeds Feel.ReducedMotion (today a manual toggle only). No speech audio, so no captions; audio has a mute and volumes already.

## Seams to request (upstream-owned, not sent)
Controls-sheet provider in ClickToPlayOverlay; LMB to UseFocused; programmatic release without the 1 s cooldown; reduced-motion default from the OS.

## Cut
12-row controls sheet, welcome and blurb toasts, 'Built with Unity' on the Manor loader, 3D in-world map.

## Uncertain
Esc re-lock behaviour and the Unity string-return marshalling were not tested; confirm in implementation.

decisions.topic: Rewind and checkpoints across zones: pin rule, no WorldHistory edit
decisions.choice: A zone may be unloaded only if it is not current, not StartZone, not WorldHistory.LastCheckpoint.Zone and no entry in WorldHistory.Changes has Pose.Zone == that zone. Placement undo is a stack pop in ProjectionSystem, and records null-check their destroyed objects, so rewinding after an unload does not throw. The real danger is a rebuilt pristine zone overlapping pasted pieces that live in the global PlacedPhotos root; the pin rule makes that state unreachable.

decisions.topic: Painting World loading: one at a time, hidden under the portal fade
decisions.choice: Entering a painting is a Teleporter inside a frame whose onEnter is GoToZone(worldIndex, spawn). GoToRoom/GoToZone call EnsureBuilt(i) at the fade's peak (the move already happens there), then SetCurrentZone, then UnloadIdle(keep: i). Exit is a portal back to the Painting Wing at that frame's spawn. Targets: build + bake <= 300 ms (hard cap 500 ms) at the opaque peak; unload <= 50 ms. The load beat is the existing 0.40 s fade; tint it with the painting's key colour.
decisions.why: Room.Build is synchronous and Web has no exceptions or threads, so the honest design hides one hitch behind full opacity instead of pretending to slice it. Prebuilding on approach is cut. The millisecond targets are unmeasured estimates; the seam logs per-zone build and unload times so the first Unity run measures them.

decisions.topic: Memory on unload: unload helper plus Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets, not blind mesh destroy
decisions.choice: UnloadZone SetActive(false) then Destroy the zone root's children and the diorama root, calls ZoneCatalog.Create(key) for a fresh Room and a fresh RoomContext on rebuild (Room.Solutions is an append-only readonly list, so a Room instance cannot be built twice), then Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets() under the fade. Baked meshes are NOT destroyed one by one.

recon.docMarkdown:
# M12 Streaming and performance: up/zone-streaming

North star v1.1. Recon only: nothing was run in Unity, and every unmeasured number is labelled as an estimate.

## Verdict

Seam, not rewrite. Zones keep their slots (x = i*50), indices and checkpoint ids. Only the cost of filling a slot moves from boot to first entry. Streaming is off in the Editor and every test, so each existing test sees today's boot.

## The seam

- Room.Load: Eager (default) | Lazy | Unloadable.
- ZoneCatalog.Streaming (default false; PortfolioRegistrar sets it for the Web player only) and ZoneCatalog.Create(key), which returns a fresh Room from the stored factory.
- GameBootstrap: BuildZone(i) and CaptureZone(i) are extracted from the boot loops. New: EnsureBuilt, IsBuilt, BuildAll, IsPinned, UnloadIdle, plus ZoneBuilt and ZoneUnloaded events.
- GoToRoom, GoToZone and OnCheckpointRestored call EnsureBuilt. Restart calls OnRestart only on built zones, then unloads.
- Files: Room.cs, ZoneCatalog.cs, GameBootstrap.cs (all upstream-owned, so a seam), one hook in IonPlayTestBase, new StreamingPlayTests, and a one-line registrar change in the fork.

## What streams

- Eager: Foyer, Grand Gallery and the core six. Hub and the ending read other zones' diorama photos every 0.5 s.
- Lazy: Hall of Honours, Camera Room, Arcade, Painting Wing.
- Unloadable: each Painting World.

## Rewind across zones

WorldHistory keeps one checkpoint and stamps every change with the player's zone. A zone unloads only when it is not current, not the start zone, not the checkpoint zone, and has no change in WorldHistory.Changes. Placement undo is a stack pop and its records null-check destroyed objects, so no change to WorldHistory or ProjectionSystem is needed. The real danger was a pristine rebuilt zone overlapping pasted pieces in the global PlacedPhotos root; the pin rule makes that unreachable.

## Photos

PhotoData owns its clipped meshes and uses shared Palette materials, so a photo taken inside a Painting World outlives it. You can carry a piece of the painting into the Manor. Teleporter registry entries are never removed. Phase 1 supports no diorama shots in streamed rooms; a streamed room that registers shots is forced Eager with a logged error.

## Painting Worlds

One loaded at a time. A frame is a portal; the build happens at the fade's opaque peak, then the previous world unloads. Target 300 ms build, 500 ms hard cap, 50 ms unload (estimates; the seam logs real numbers). A world needs a public parameterless constructor, a Build that works with ctx.Game == null, and at least one Walk solution. Lay it out along Z, within +-25 m in X.

## Budgets (measured, last test run)

| Zone | batches | tris |
|---|---|---|
| t1 | 87 | 30,266 |
| t2 | 80 | 17,040 |
| hub | 108 | 36,704 |
| stairs | 100 | 28,070 |
| camera | 97 | 23,778 |
| gallery | 78 | 37,272 |
| pf.foyer | 73 | 18,664 |
| pf.gallery | 63 | 40,292 |

Limits stay 120 and 60k, frozen. New zones design to 100 and 50k, because Ultra twins and new Mats each add a batch. Add the missing local-light test: at most 8 enabled, Ultra only.

## Download diet (measured)

First visit is about 18.0 MB on the wire (wasm 8.01 MB, data 9.96 MB, live, gzip). Raw: wasm 22.0 MB, data 15.3 MB.

1. Unused URP FilmGrain x10 and SMAA textures, about 2.8 MB raw: null them via up/web-diet.
2. Music 3.9 MB source ogg: spike on-demand fetch; the Foyer currently plays the game's rooms.ogg (2.2 MB) because AreaOfRoomName falls through to Puzzle.
3. MCP for Unity: 29 KB in the player; strip it from release builds anyway.
4. Front Door prefetches on 'Enter the Manor' intent.
5. Cut: brotli (16.3 vs 18.2 MB, and Pages serves gzip), wasm tuning (already DiskSizeLTO, strip High, no exceptions).

## Risks and mitigations

- Unbuilt zone fails existing audits: default off, plus BuildAll in the new fixtures.
- Mesh leak: Geo shares cached meshes, so use UnloadUnusedAssets and a mesh-count test; fall back to tagging at ArchBake.cs:402.
- New zone draws for one frame: ApplyZoneCulling runs inside EnsureBuilt.
- Static Room.Solutions: rebuild creates a fresh Room.
- Style leak: BuildZone restores ArchKit.Style.
- Web has no exceptions: a failing Build cannot be caught, same as boot.

## Order

up/palette and up/zone-streaming in parallel. up/lens after streaming. Stack zone-streaming on zone-catalog; the orchestrator confirms.

## Defer

Core-six streaming (photo bank, gated on measurement), diorama capture for streamed zones, prebuild on approach, brotli.

decisions.topic: Shader light pools on every tier
decisions.choice: up/palette adds 8 global light pools to FlatToon ForwardLit (_IonPoolPos[8], _IonPoolCol[8], _IonPoolInfo), toon-banded with half-lambert wrap and applied before fog. A fork-only feeder, Look/ManorGlow, picks the nearest N (Low 4, Medium and High 8, Ultra 8 minus active real lights) with smoothed fades. Flicker is ±8% from smooth noise at 6-8 Hz; under reduced motion there is no flicker, only breathing under 0.5 Hz of ±3%. decisions.choice: Five primes: 16 mm, 28 mm (the default, identical to today's 50 degree capture), 50, 85 and 135 mm. LensKit.ViewFovFor keeps the view at 70 degrees for the default lens. Camera-mode controls: wheel = lens, Q/E = aperture, F = film, with photo selection and rotation suppressed in camera mode. Five original-named film looks (Standard, Candle, Vivid, Mono, Cyanotype) live in IonGrade and bake into the print. An X-T5-style viewmodel sits on layer 8. The instax-proportioned print develops over 2.4 s through a fork Ion/PrintDevelop shader. The lens collection persists in PlayerPrefs. Capture-time accumulation DoF comes last (Low 0, Medium 4, High 8, Ultra 12 samples). Cut: the exposure triangle, continuous zoom, manual focus, live DoF and the rear LCD.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for variable aperture, zooms, colour spaces, an X-T5-style body, collectable lenses and a lightweight print-film animation. The 50 degree pins (CriticFixTests.cs:46-51, RoomSolutionTests.cs:126) survive. The URP depth texture is off, so accumulation DoF needs no depth sampling.

# Manor plan: Track M (M-Manager, north star v1.1)

One plan built from seven recon reports. Numbers marked (est.) have not been measured. Crew briefs carry the detail.

## The Manor in one line
A candlelit royal home of five rooms on one spine, with the Grand Gallery always one step away.

## Spine and rooms
- **The spine:** Foyer → **Grand Gallery** (the only hub) → Hall of Honours. A second branch runs Gallery → Camera Room → Painting Wing → world.
- **Distance:** no room is more than three doors from the Gallery, and every other room has a [ GRAND GALLERY ] pad within 3 m of where you arrive.
- **Curve:** welcome, anticipation, reverence, curiosity, wonder, play.
- **Cut:** the Workshop, the Study and a separate Arcade zone.

| Room | Key · order · x | Size (m) | Holds | Its one moment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Foyer | pf.foyer · 1000 · 300 | 18×24×6 | name, monogram stele, contact bureau, game door | candles wake in a wave; light the desk candle and the contact letter appears |
| Grand Gallery | pf.gallery · 1010 · 350 | 15×48×6, three bays | 8 projects, robot/CAD statue, arcade bay | the two strongest works meet you in bay 1; the statue waits on the axis |
| Hall of Honours | pf.honours · 1020 · 400 | 16×40×9, apse | DECA glass hero, ≤6 award plinths, medal gantry | the hero, top-lit in the apse, first seen from a brass inlay 10 m away |
| Camera Room | pf.lens · 1030 · 450 | 16×28×6 | X-T5 monument, camera stand, 4 lenses, 3 films, sample prints | raise the camera and the room turns into the film stock; the print develops |
| Painting Wing | pf.wing · 1040 · 500 | 12×34×7 | framed portals (1 at launch) | step on the inlay and the frame takes you in (G) |

Worlds are G zones from order 1100. URL aliases are honours, lens/lenses and wing; `?zone=camera` still means the puzzle wing.

## Exhibit grammar
- **Display types:**
  - frame = project;
  - plinth statue = robot/CAD (Gallery) or award (Hall);
  - gantry = medals;
  - lens plinth = lens;
  - easel = print;
  - cabinet = playable demo;
  - stele = monogram.
- **One verb:** **E reads** (range 4.5 m) and opens the DOM wall label. No turning statues, turntables or coin drops.
- **Content:** slots are built from lists, so nothing empty exists, and every unknown is `[PLACEHOLDER: …]`. Today's `projects.json` ("Project One", year "2026") is unmarked and is fixed first.
- **Heroes:** code-built with HeroKit on PropBuild/Arch, plus the fork's Frustum and ClippedHull. The DECA glass is self-lit Frost with brass bracket clips: it glows without transparency. Build order is DECA, gantry, camera monument, robot. Blender waits.

## Look: dim candles, not orange mud
- **One mood per room** in ManorLook:
  - Ambient fill is set *after* `ZoneMood.Make`. Make lifts ambient 55% toward white, which is why today's fill is grey.
  - Fog fades to cool plum-blue. Warm light lives only in pools and flame cores.
  - The Foyer is the brightest room and the Wing the only cool one. The Camera Room is a warm darkroom with one cool Frost table.
- **Candles have jobs:**
  - one chandelier per bay;
  - one candelabra per exhibit;
  - sconces only at doors.
- **Real lights:** Ultra lights only on chandeliers, candelabras and pads, at half today's intensity. Sconces lose theirs.
- **Shader pools (up/palette):** the nearest 8 candle pools light every tier (4 on Low). Flicker is ±8% smooth; under reduced motion there is none. Every room must still read with pools and lights off.
- **New Mats:** Gilt 24 (metal-ramp finish), Marble 25 (+Pat.Marble 18), Velvet 26 (sheen), Flame 27. Glass, Silver and Crystal are deferred.
- **Who wears what:** Brass stays for plaques, markers and the accent. Gilt goes on frames and candelabras, and Velvet on the carpets. The Gallery floor stays oak.

## Camera (up/lens, then M-C3)
- **Lenses:** five primes: 16, **28 (default, the same as today)**, 50, 85 and 135 mm. `ViewFovFor` keeps the view at 70° for the default lens, so the existing pins hold.
- **Controls:** wheel = lens, Q/E = aperture, F = film.
- **Film looks:** five, under original names, live in IonGrade and bake into the print.
- **Viewmodel and print:** an X-T5-style viewmodel on layer 8, and an instax-proportioned print that develops over 2.4 s.
- **Collection and DoF:** collected lenses persist in PlayerPrefs. Capture-time DoF comes last.
- **Cut:** the exposure triangle, zoom, manual focus and live DoF.

## Overlay and onboarding (M-C5)
- **Loader:** restyled by compose-time injection with `--ion-*` tokens. It shows three control rows, "Enter the Manor" and "Go straight to the Grand Gallery". Its first focusable item is "Read everything as a page".
- **Map:** **M** opens a DOM "Plan of the house" (an SVG plan plus a real list), with the Gallery first.
- **One overlay slot:** label, plan and arcade share one `window.ionOverlay` slot.
- **Accessibility:** focus trap and return, browser Back, and a live region. The OS reduced-motion setting seeds `Feel.ReducedMotion` through its existing setter, so no seam is needed.
- **Deleted:** the toasts and the 12-row controls wall.

## Streaming and download (up/zone-streaming, then M-C6)
- **The seam:** additive and off in the Editor and tests.
- **Load classes:**
  - Eager: Foyer, Gallery, Camera Room (its prints are diorama shots) and the core six;
  - Lazy: Hall and Wing;
  - Unloadable: worlds, under a pin rule taken from WorldHistory's single checkpoint.
- **Download:** the first visit measured 18.0 MB. up/web-diet removes the unused URP FilmGrain and SMAA textures (about 2.8 MB raw). A music-fetch spike follows.

## Seams, in order (one Seams crew, one at a time)
1. **up/lens:** InstantCamera, ViewfinderFrame, FirstPersonController, PhotoHolder, PhotoOverlayUI, Feel (partial), IonAtmosphere.hlsl, ProjectionSystem.RenderInto.
2. **up/palette:** Surface, Palette, FlatToon (finish + pools), IonPattern, IonAudio.Footsteps, EditMode tests.
3. **up/zone-streaming:** Room, ZoneCatalog (+SetLoad), GameBootstrap, IonPlayTestBase hook, StreamingPlayTests.
4. **up/manor-ux:** IonPointerLock cooldown flag, template skip hook, ClickToPlayOverlay sheet provider, Manor return from HubLightTable/GalleryEnding, LMB behind a flag.
5. **up/web-diet:** URP global settings asset.

**Why not lens → streaming → palette:**
- By the recon file lists these seams share no file, so the order follows unblock value.
- up/lens is on G's critical path.
- up/palette unblocks the look crew and the final exhibit materials.
- No development crew waits on streaming: doors call `GoToZone`, which gets `EnsureBuilt` inside the seam, and tests run with streaming off.
- The orchestrator confirms the order.

## Crews and order
1. **M-F** (split, stubs, contracts, content v2).
2. In parallel: **M-QA** (TourShots, budget JSON, route and fact guards), **M-C1 Exhibits**, **M-C2 Rooms** and **M-C5 Overlay**.
3. **Gate G3a slice:** the Hall with the DECA hero, plaque and label, approved by the owner.
4. Then, as their seams land:
   - **M-C4 Look** (moods now, pools and Mats after up/palette);
   - **M-C3 Camera** (after up/lens);
   - **M-C6 Streaming** (after up/zone-streaming).

The Seams crew starts on day one.

## Budgets (design caps under the frozen 120 / 60k)
| Zone | Batches | Tris | Basis |

| Foyer | 85 | 24k | measured 73 / 18,664 |
| Gallery | 80 | 47k | measured 63 / 40,292 |
| Hall | 95 | 50k | shell ≤83 + heroes 12 (est.) |
| Camera Room | 85 | 40k | est. |
| Wing | 75 | 35k | est. |

At most 8 Ultra lights are enabled anywhere, and uGUI plaques count as draws. Evidence is TourShots PNG + JSON (Low, Ultra, lights off) at the PR SHA.

## Delete first under pressure
1. Capture DoF.
2. The Bedroom world (G).
3. Fold the Camera Room into a Wing vestibule.
4. Halve the Hall plinths.
5. Drop pools on Low.
6. Drop the Velvet sheen.

# The Starry Night pilot: level design (G01)

North star v1.1. Read-only recon; every number is an estimate until a Unity run (my frustum math is measured in `portfolio-evidence/wave1a/g01-pilot/frustum_check.py`).

## The idea

Not a diorama: a 3-minute climb up the painting. You arrive in the dark foreground beside the cypress. The sky moves. High upper right, where the painting has its crescent, a gilt frame glows on a physical moon. You can see where you are going from the first frame. Two photos get you there.

## Beats

1. **0:00 Arrive (identity).** Toast "The Starry Night. Saint-Rémy, 1889." Cypress rising off the top left, lit village and spire under ultramarine hills, 10 stars and Venus, the moon with its door.
2. **0:20 The handed photo (Place 1).** An easel holds a pre-made photo of a flame-tier ladder up the 3 m hill. Stand on the brass marker, raise, place. Teaches placing.
3. **0:50 Too high.** A second wall (6 m). Hint: "Too high. The sky behind you was climbing."
4. **1:10 Your own photo (Snap, Place 2).** Back on the ridge, turn around: a spiral stair climbs the back hill. Snap it from the marker facing away. Return to H1 and place it into the wall: the wall is carved, the stair and a wide deck arrive.
5. **2:00 Climb.** Spiral, deck, moon stair, crescent platform.
6. **2:40 Exit frame.** Step into the gilt frame in the moon's hollow: back to the Manor.

## Layout (room-local, floor y=0, +Z forward)

| Element | Position |
|---|---|
| Spawn / easel | (0,0,2) / (4.5,0,2) |
| T0 ridge, cypress | z -10..13; cypress (-10,0,4), 22 m |
| Ladder (pre-made delta) | x 7.25..9.75, z 7..13, 12 steps |
| H1, H2 | y=3 z 13..31; y=9 z 31..42 |
| Spiral stair | axis (0,*,-5), r 3, 24 steps, rise 6; deck y=6, z -12..-9.5 |
| Moon stair / crescent | x 15.25..17.5, z 41 to 29; platform y=15, z 20..29 |
| Exit frame | (14.5,15,22.5) |

Sky dome (non-Sliceable): stars at roughly (x%,y%) from the painting: 10,4 / 23,3 / 34,4 / 41,6 / 24,17 / 61,8 / 70,23 / 32,33 / 13,48 / 5,45; Venus 35,53; moon 90,17.

## Solutions (Place/Snap each have a marker)

pickup easel -> **Place** ladder (8.5,0,3.5) yaw 0 photo 0 -> goal H1 (8.5,3,16) -> walk W2 base (Blocked) -> **Snap** (0,0,12) yaw 180 -> **Place** (0,3,18) yaw 0, latest -> goals: deck, crescent -> teleport exit to the gallery. All pitch 0.

## Why it solves

Frustum check: the snap holds all 75 sampled stair points at pitch -3/0/+3 and x +-0.3. After Place 2 the moon stair, crescent and exit are outside the cone at roll 0 and 90, so nothing needed is cut. Neither marker's frustum reaches the Grand Gallery. Ladder Place goes first because the pre-made photo contains the whole forward cone and would revert the swirl.

## Default camera

All solved with the 50 degree, 4:3 camera at pitch 0. Wide lens and film looks are optional garnish only.

## Budget (estimate)

60-85 batches, 5-7k triangles. Ultra-only: sky drift, bloom, 4 of 8 lights. Bake chunk 16.

## Codas

Café Terrace: cut (two checkpoints instead). Bedroom in Arles: defer as its own ~20-batch world.

- **Pitch error at the junction:** +-3 degrees at 22 m is about 1.1 m. Mitigate with stepped shoulders, or shorten the rise to 4.5 m. Run Forgiveness early.

# Painting Worlds ranking (g03-worlds, north star v1.1)

## The rule that shapes every trick
A photo in this engine is a rigid 3D slice of geometry, not an image. Capture slices every Sliceable in the frustum. Place deletes whatever the viewer's frustum sees, deactivates Interactables inside it, then pastes the slice at the viewer's pose with the player's roll (0-360). No scale change. The sky and Backdrop are never captured. So a Witness-style 'gap closes from one viewpoint' puzzle will not work. What does work: translation, roll, overwrite, FOV-shaped slabs, and removal of devices. (ProjectionSystem.cs:348-420; PhotoHolder.cs:54,292; art-bible.md:64-65.)

## Ranking
Scores out of 20 for trippiness, mechanic clarity, cheapness and engine fit (my judgement):

| # | World | Score | Verb |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Water Lilies, "No Horizon" | 18 | roll 180 turns a reflection into a floor |
| 2 | Garden of Earthly Delights, "Graft" | 17 | paste erases: graft Eden over Hell |
| 3 | The Great Wave, "Bring the Mountain" | 15 | telephoto slab brings Fuji to you |
| 4 | Cyanotype Ferns, "Contact Print" | 13 | close-range photograms |
| Fraud | The Imaginary Prisons (Piranesi) | 17 | three lies, each broken once |

**1. Water Lilies.** A mirrored double pond with no horizon: pads above, mirror copies below. Photograph the reflection looking down and paste with roll 180. That rotation about the view axis lifts the reflected pads above the line of sight, faces up, so you climb a staircase made from reflections. Pads are 12-gon prisms (about 44 tris each, derived), so the whole zone is probably under 8k tris and 40 batches (estimate). Look: existing Mats only (Lilac, Mint, Rose, Foliage tints), heavy fog, sky and fog the same value. Risk: no translucent water Mat; fallback is holes in an opaque floor. Mirror copies must be left-right symmetric because roll also flips x (untested).

**2. Bosch.** A triptych along Z: Eden, Garden, Hell. The verb is overwrite. Photograph a clean Eden meadow and paste it over a Hell tile. Existing engine only. Keep the imagery to giant fruit, birds, glass spheres and ice; no torture scenes. Estimate: up to 30k tris, 70 batches. Primitives (spheres as 12-gons, wedges) keep it cheap.

**3. Great Wave.** Telephoto captures a narrow deep slab (far plane 250 m). Shoot Fuji through the curl, paste it at your feet, and the tiny mountain becomes a ramp. Claws are wedges (8 tris), boats are Mover platforms over a void. About 12k tris (estimate). **Blocked on the lens feature (task #11);** until then it is only a skin.

**4. Atkins.** Fern silhouettes as thin slabs; a close capture pastes them as contact prints. Strongest tie to Mat.Cyanotype and the camera heritage, weakest twist, and it needs a film look that does not exist. Build as a short coda, not a level.

## Fraud-style world: The Imaginary Prisons
Piranesi's Carceri (1750, 1761, public domain) with vault arches, stairs and fog. Cut faces already show section hatch, so every paste is drawn as engraver's cross-hatch (not on the Low tier). Three lies, each broken once (the only Fraud idea the sources support):
1. **False floor:** a decoy landing built as a device. Any paste whose frustum holds it removes it, revealing the true route. Pasting reveals, not only builds.
2. **Inverted vault:** a ceiling stair photographed upside-down and pasted with roll 180 becomes a floor stair.
3. **Cutting your way back:** a paste overwrites the stair behind you. Documented rewind returns you to the near side, and falls already exist (limbo, gravity 15 percent, [R]).
Gravity cannot flip: only a scalar Gravity exists (FirstPersonController.cs:81,235). The world must lie through geometry, not gravity. Estimate: up to 40k tris, 70 batches. The title avoids the game's name.

## Engine needs
| Need | Exists? |
|---|---|
| Roll 0-360 | yes |
| Overwrite and device removal | yes |
| Rewind to pose | yes |
| Streaming | **no**: every zone is built at boot, then culled |
| Lens or zoom | **no**: capture FOV is a constant 50 degrees (InstantCamera.cs:23) |
| Film looks | **no**: the grade is global |
| Mirrors | no (build mirrored geometry) |
| Gravity direction | no |
| Translucent Mat | no |
Test limit: placement frusta must not touch neighbouring zones (50 m spacing), so keep content within about 100 m of Z and fog the far end.

## Rights (flag for g04)
Hokusai, Piranesi, Monet, Bosch, Atkins, Klimt: public domain (secondary sources; museum-scan licence unverified). Mondrian: pre-1929 safe; the Mondrian Trust disputes some 1930 works. No painting pixels are used, so exposure is mostly the print preview and titles.

## Cut
Drop Klimt first (new pattern codes, no perception twist), then Mondrian, Op Art, Melting Time (duplicates rewind, Dali in copyright). Day over Night survives only as a sky-versus-ambient look trick. Great Wave and Atkins wait for lenses and film looks.

## Uncertain
Nothing was run in Unity: costs are estimates. The roll-180 trick needs a prototype.

# g05-look: Painting World look spec (v1.1)

**Verdict.** Impasto is a fork-only shader (Ion/PaintToon) and the sky is a camera-relative dome with its own shader. Neither touches an upstream file, adds a texture or changes the FlatToon vertex layout. A recon sketch is at portfolio-evidence/wave1a/g05-look/paint-sketch.hlsl (unverified, not compiled).

## Impasto
- Copy FlatToon into Assets/Portfolio/Resources/Portfolio/. ForwardLit gains a paint block after the pattern multiply. The other three passes are copied verbatim. Same CBUFFER with 8 floats appended, so SRP Batcher holds. UsePass would break that.
- Each room clones Palette.Get(mat) per Mat at the end of Build, before Arch.Bake, keeping the Ion_Mat_ name prefix (footsteps still work). Batches stay one per Mat.
- Strokes: two staggered cell layers. Each layer: one hash, a jittered centre, a flow direction taken at the cell centre, a tapered capsule anti-aliased with fwidth. Flow is analytic (three vortices plus wind) in four modes: DAB ground, SWIRL hills, FLAME cypress, DASH village. Colour is the Mat colour with per-stroke value and hue variation and a bristle streak. Optional ridge light is screen-space ddx/ddy of stroke height against the sun.
- Anchoring: coordinates come from pattern space only, converted to zone-local (subtract i*50, or i*200 and +1000 in y, for dioramas). No time, no screen position, no world axes. Strokes cannot swim.

## Capture parity
Photos and pastes use the same shader and the same shared material (ProjectionSystem.cs:214). Pattern space travels through cut, merge and paste. Tier changes only fade distance, bristle and ridge, never layout. Rolled pastes are safe because nothing uses world axes. Tests to add: PaintParity (preview vs paste, mean difference under 1.5/255 outside the cut) and a zone-local constants test.

## Sky dome
- 16x8 inverted sphere, about 224 tris, one batch, child of the zone root. Vertex shader puts it at the camera at 300 m and collapses it unless the camera is in its own zone or diorama footprint.
- Queue Geometry+100, ZWrite off, ZTest LEqual: early-Z skips terrain, and it overdraws the Backdrop ring (640-800 m) with no seam. Not Sliceable.
- Colour: gradient from IonSkyColor (so fog matches) plus two stroke layers on three analytic vortices. Slow animation: rotate the lookup about the main vortex (omega about 0.04 rad/s) and pulse star halos about 6%. Reduced motion freezes both.
- Ten stars, Venus and a crescent moon from a 12-entry array traced from the evidence JPG. Core #C4CB8E, rings #AFB270 and #B5BE9D, in 12 radial dabs. Ultra bloom: multiply cores by 1+_IonUltraFx.w, the sun-disc hook.

## Ribbons
About 90 oriented boxes (about 1,080 tris) per world, as closed convex elements, baked with BakeLocal under a rotating parent, flagged Soft|Dynamic. Capture clips at the current angle, so the in-frame part freezes into static pieces while the cut remainder (same parent) keeps turning. Local pattern space rotates with it, so strokes stay glued.

Tiers: Low layer A only. Medium both layers. High bristle, ridge, halo rings. Ultra star bloom.

## Costs (all estimates, nothing run)
- Impasto: about 100 extra ALU on painted pixels within about 30 m, zero beyond the fade.
- Sky: about 180 ALU full-screen at High, about 1 to 1.5 ms on an integrated GPU at 1080p; about 0.4 ms on Low. Drawn after opaques so terrain pixels skip it.
- Geometry: dome 224 plus ribbons about 1,080 tris and 2 batches, far inside 60k and 120.

## Hooks
A fork component on ZoneChanged turns Ambience clouds and sun glow off in painting worlds (restoring the player's values) and feeds _IonPaintQ.

## Cut first
Ridge light if it aliases, Ultra daub geometry, curl-noise or flow-map textures, hue variation, a new Pat id.

## Uncertain
Soft|Dynamic acceptance by Validate; the dome vertex-collapse gating under batching; ridge-light aliasing at 3 px strokes. All need a one-day Unity spike.

decisions.topic: What the Starry Night pilot is
decisions.choice: A three-minute climb up the painting, not a diorama. The goal is in sight from the first frame: a gilt exit frame in the crescent moon's hollow, upper right. There are exactly two photo puzzles: a handed photo (it pastes a cypress whose flame tiers are steps up the 3 m hill), then your own photo (snap the spiral stair on the back hill facing -Z, paste it into the 6 m wall from the H1 marker). Then a plain walk: stair, belvedere deck, moon stair, crescent, exit. G01's layout, markers and solution list are adopted, except where G-D004 changes them.
decisions.rationale: A goal you can see makes the level finishable by non-gamers in 3 to 10 minutes. One new verb per puzzle (place a given photo, then take your own) repeats the proven StairsWing to CameraWing escalation. The camera is the only way up, so the level shows the camera off, and the painting gives it its identity.
alternatives: Walk-through diorama with no puzzle
Plan sketch: a rotating ribbon frozen into a walkable spiral as the main puzzle
Three or more puzzles including a moon Snap/Place
decisions.budgetImpact: G01 estimate 60-85 batches, 5-7k triangles; locked targets in G-D011

decisions.topic: Photo grammar every world must obey
decisions.choice: Design to the engine's real rule. A photo is a rigid 3D slice. Place deletes the viewer's frustum (cutting Sliceables and deactivating devices whose pivot is inside) and pastes at worldPose = viewerPoseRolled x capturePose^-1 x piece. There is no scale change and no forced-perspective closing through photos. Poses are level: Snap and Place both snap pitch to 0 within 5 degrees. Anything needed after a Place must lie outside that solution's cone, or also be built in the diorama so the paste re-creates it.
decisions.rationale: Verified in source: ProjectionSystem.cs:194-218 (capture), :397-405 (device removal), :408-420 (rigid paste); PhotoHolder.cs:29 LevelSnapDegrees 5, applied at PhotoHolder.cs:411,482 and InstantCamera.cs:168. Two G03 proposals break this rule (see conflicts).
alternatives: Allow scale/forced-perspective tricks (needs an engine change; out of scope)
decisions.budgetImpact: none

decisions.topic: The swirl: critical path vs sky vs ribbons
decisions.choice: (a) The critical path is a static Solid spiral stair: 24 four-sided prisms with yaw, 0.25 m rise each, 6 m total. It is built through PropBuild with B.Exempt so the off-grid yawed treads pass Arch.Validate. (b) The swirl, the 10 stars, Venus and the crescent are drawn by a non-Sliceable SwirlSky dome, so a photo never cuts them. (c) Three Soft rotating ribbons ('photograph the wind', down from G05's five) go through a one-day G-C2 spike with kill criteria. A walkable frozen ribbon is deferred.
decisions.rationale: Source shows capture already freezes non-device Sliceables at their current matrix and parents photo pieces to a static root (ProjectionSystem.cs:194-218, 1287-1292), and BakeLocal accepts non-Interactable Dynamic pieces (ArchBake.cs:44-50, 247-250). So no photo-clone seam is needed, which corrects G01. But a time-driven ribbon on the critical path would make RunAll and Forgiveness non-deterministic and add moving colliders, so it stays optional.
alternatives: Plan: frozen rotating ribbon as the walkable puzzle
G01: no ribbons at all
G05: five Soft ribbons in v1
decisions.budgetImpact: Dome 1 batch about 224 tris; ribbons at most 2 batches about 650 tris; stair about 288 tris

# Painting Worlds: G-Manager lock (north star v1.1)

Read-only judgement of the four Wave 1a recons (G01 pilot, G03 worlds, G04 rights, G05 look). Every disputed claim was re-checked in source; seven changed the plan.

## Verdict

The Starry Night pilot is a three-minute climb, not a diorama. You arrive in the dark foreground. A gilt exit frame glows in the crescent moon, upper right, and you can see it from the first frame. Two photos get you there. A handed photo pastes a cypress whose flame tiers are steps. Then you turn round, snap the spiral stair on the back hill and paste it into the 6 m wall. Everything solves with the default 50 degree, 4:3 camera at roll 0. The pilot needs no streaming, lenses, film looks or new Mats.

## What the source changed

1. **Freezing already works.** Capture clips non-device Sliceables at their current matrix and parents photo pieces to a static root (ProjectionSystem.cs:194-218, 1287-1292). No photo-clone seam is needed. Rotating ribbons are possible, but stay off the critical path.
2. **Pitch is assisted.** Snap and Place both snap to level within 5 degrees (PhotoHolder.cs:29, 411, 482; InstantCamera.cs:168). G01's 1.1 m junction error mostly disappears. Yaw error remains and gets a Forgiveness test.
3. **The cypress was out of frame.** At (-10,0,4) it sits about 79 degrees left of the spawn view; the player sees about 51 degrees either side (70 degree vertical FOV, 16:9). Move it to about 40 degrees left, near (-6,0,9), and re-run the frustum check.
4. **Deep links skip OnEnter.** Only GoToZoneWorld calls it (GameBootstrap.cs:351), so `?zone=` and test starts would have no camera. A CameraPickup on the easel grants it; the OnEnter unlock stays as a fallback.
5. **Ultra twins must not be cloned.** `Palette.IsUltra` is a reference set (Palette.cs:308). A PaintToon clone of an Ultra material would draw off Ultra, so the swap skips them.
6. **Chunk size.** A placement re-cooks every chunk it cuts (ArchBake.cs:28-32). Keep the 8 m default; raise it only if measured batches demand it and Place stays within 25 ms.
7. **Neighbours show.** Zone culling still draws the next zone's collider batches 50 m away (GameBootstrap.cs:386). Edge hills hide them until streaming lands.

## The pilot, locked

| Time | Beat |
|---|---|
| 0:00 | Arrive: cypress left rising off the top, lit village and spire low right, 10 stars and Venus, the crescent with its frame. Toast: "The Starry Night. Saint-Remy, 1889." |
| 0:20 | Take the camera and photo at the easel; place the cypress ladder from the brass marker |
| 0:50 | A 6 m wall; the hint points behind you |
| 1:10 | Snap the spiral stair facing -Z; place it from the H1 marker |
| 2:00 | Climb the stair, deck, moon stair and crescent |
| 2:40 | The gilt frame returns you to the Grand Gallery (the Painting Wing once it exists) |

Layout, markers and solutions are G01's, with the cypress moved. The exit is also built as a DioramaTeleporter, so a placement that swallows it re-pastes a working copy.

**Sky.** A non-Sliceable dome draws the swirl, 10 stars, Venus and the crescent, and is never cut. Star positions are traced by script from the evidence image. "Eleven" was the plan's wording, not the owner's; the sourced count stands.

**Ribbons.** Three Soft rotating ribbons ("photograph the wind") are a one-day G-C2 spike. They are cut if Validate rejects Soft plus Dynamic, if a Place that cuts them exceeds 25 ms, or if a reviewed filmstrip of the two solution placements looks accidental. A walkable frozen ribbon is deferred.

**Look.** Fork-only PaintToon twins (same Mats, same UV0, one CBUFFER) plus the dome. Existing Mats only; the cypress is Graphite under the night mood. G05's darkening multiplier is cut as a local colour hack. Tiers trim cost, never stroke layout. Reduced motion freezes sky and ribbons.

**Targets (measured, not estimated):** at most 90 batches, 20k triangles and 4 of the 8 Ultra lights; Place within 25 ms.

**Codas.** Cafe Terrace is cut (two checkpoints instead). Bedroom in Arles is deferred to its own small world; its illusion is geometry, not a photo trick.

## Art-bible scope

Painting Worlds may break the upstream look rules 2, 6 and 7 (right angles, off-white structure, no black), as the Manor already does. They keep every absolute limit: no textures, UV0 through Arch.Bake, Lead A's Mats, the zone budgets. The orchestrator logs this.

## Next worlds, ranked

1. **The Imaginary Prisons** (Piranesi, Carceri). The owner asked for a Fraud-style world. Three lies, each broken once: a decoy device floor that a paste removes, a ceiling stair rolled 180 degrees into a floor, a paste that cuts your way back. Existing engine only.
2. **Water Lilies, "No Horizon"** (Monet). Roll 180 turns a reflection into a floor; the cheapest world. Correction: capture and place level, because at -30 degrees of pitch the flip leaves pads tilted 60 degrees. Ship after 2027-01-01 (life plus 100).
3. **Garden of Earthly Delights, "Graft"** (Bosch), cut to two panels. Paste Eden over Hell; no torture imagery.
4. **The Great Wave** (Hokusai), after the lens seam and with a new verb. A paste is rigid, so "Fuji at your feet" cannot work; telephoto must earn its place as a narrow, surgical slab.

Cut: Klimt, Mondrian (the Trust's January 2026 dispute), Op Art, Melting Time, Day over Night. Atkins waits for film looks, as a coda.

## Rights

US public domain: published 1930 or earlier until 2027-01-01, then 1931. Museum CC0 first, Commons PD-Art second. Scans are reference only and never become textures in the build. Public-domain artists are credited on wall labels with their museum; inspired-by artists are never named in public.

## Crews

- G-C1 (pilot) and G-C2 (look kit) run in parallel after M-F. G-C2 first lands a no-op `PaintLook.Apply`.
- G-C3 (portals) follows the streaming seam, the Wing shell and G-C1.
